turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Welcome, thanks. Ready when you are.
What time did you go to bed last night?
Went to bed around 9:30, a bit later than usual actually — I got caught up watching a match that ran long, so maybe closer to 10.
Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? Would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

Slept about six and a half hours or so, give or take. I'd say it was fine — nothing special, just normal sleep. Woke up once around 2am for the bathroom but went right back down, so it didn't really throw things off.
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed, and why did you choose to do that activity?
Went with reading a bit — a few pages of a paperback under a lamp. Kind of a wind-down habit for me, keeps me off the phone before bed.
That sounds like a nice routine. What was the book you were reading, and what made you pick that one up?
"Nothing fancy, just a used western I picked up — Louis L'Amour, I think. Doesn't take much brainpower before bed, which is kind of the point."
Thanks for explaining that. Moving on, over the past two weeks, what factors have most affected your sleep quality?

Not much has really changed, if I'm honest — the schedule's the schedule, and I've been on it long enough that it mostly runs itself. If anything, Sunday nights are the one spot where I notice it, just a bit of a lighter sleep before the week kicks back off, but that's been true for years, not really a new factor.
Is that pattern pretty typical for you overall, or has anything about your sleep or routine changed recently?
Pretty typical, yeah. Nothing's really changed on my end — same shift, same routine, just an average week.
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?
"Yeah, I'd say so. It's not exciting, but it does the job — I get up, get through the shift without dragging, and that's really all I'm asking of it."
Thanks for sharing that. You've probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

That does feel about right for some folks, but honestly 7-9 hours would mean going to bed by 8 or so, and that's just not realistic with my schedule. I'm getting closer to 6.5, maybe 7 on a good night, and it's held up fine for me for years, so I don't lose sleep over the gap, so to speak.
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this too? Why or why not?
Not really, no — I keep the phone charging on the kitchen counter overnight, out of the bedroom. If I'm reading before bed it's the paperback, not a screen.
Do you regularly use social media? If so, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?

Not really into social media, no — I check the news headlines here and there, but I'm not scrolling through anything before bed. Once the paperback comes out, that's pretty much it for screens or feeds.
Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar applications)?
"No, not really — I'm not one to fiddle with that kind of thing much. Heard of them, sure, but it's not part of my routine."
Thanks, that’s helpful to know. If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?
Honestly, probably getting to bed a touch earlier on Sunday nights — that's the one night it tends to get shorter, right before the week starts back up. Otherwise I don't have much to complain about.
Given your work, studies, or daily responsibilities, do you think that change—going to bed a bit earlier on Sunday nights—would be doable? Why or why not?
Yeah, it's doable — I just have to actually turn the TV off instead of letting one game run into the next one. It's not a scheduling problem, more a discipline thing on my end.

Thanks for explaining that. Now, just a few optional background questions (feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share):

What is your age, your profession, your country of birth, your current country of residence, and—if different—when did you move?

As my persona, I'll answer the optional background question naturally.

52, warehouse inventory coordinator, born here in this country actually — grew up rural, about two hours from where I live now, moved to the city for the job back in my late twenties. Never left since.

Thanks for sharing that background, that’s all the main questions I have.

Before we wrap up, is there anything else about your sleep or evening routine that you’d like to add that we haven’t talked about?
